display.purpose: What somebody said, and what Dobby answered. The largest text on the surface; capped at 62ch.

headline.purpose: The plate — the board's own nameplate. Small on purpose; it is a label riveted to an instrument, not a page title. Same size as Label, Medium and told apart by tracking alone.

title.purpose: Device readings. The number on the board, in tabular figures.

body.purpose: The composer, and any running prose.

label-medium.purpose: Device names on the board, and the set line's placeholder.

label-small.purpose: Attribution, timestamps, steps, system lines. The record-keeping voice.

shadows.name: flap
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the entire system — there is no second one, and adding one is a change to The One Shadow Rule rather than to a component. A flap card is a physical object sitting proud of the board; without it the words look printed on rather than set into place. Everything else that wants depth takes a tonal step or a brass rule.

motion.name: flap-turn
motion.value: 300ms, keyframes perspective(340px) rotateX(-88deg) [cubic-bezier(.5,0,.7,.6)] → rotateX(9deg) at offset .68 [ease-out] → rotateX(0deg)
motion.purpose: The board's one moving part. When a state word changes, the card falls, overshoots its stop and settles, so it reads as a physical thing landing rather than a value being replaced. Driven from app.js by a MutationObserver on characterData — a flap arriving does not turn, only a word changing — and skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: mark-lean
motion.purpose: Dobby rotating −15° into the conversation when he is attending, and back upright in faint ink when he is not. Transition removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: tick-pulse
motion.value: pulse 1.1s ease-in-out infinite; @keyframes pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: .3 } 50% { opacity: 1 } }
motion.purpose: A running step's tick breathing while a tool call is in flight. Animation set to none under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: disclosure-caret
motion.purpose: The collapsed-steps caret turning when the record of a reply's work is opened.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The width at which the board fits a hand, and the system's third. The number is the feed's: its entry is five tracks, 22.5rem of them fixed, which with four gaps needs 392px before `what` — the column saying which device and which action — gets a pixel, so at 390px the column vanished and the row ran 31px into a sideways scroll. Five columns only tell the truth once `what` can hold `device · action` in the record voice, which measures 168px; 392 + 168 + the two edges is 589. Below it the entry is two lines — metadata in faint ink, substance full-width in --ink and allowed to wrap anywhere. Two other things ride the same number: the row's state column drops 9.5rem → 6rem, since below this the row is narrower than its own 34rem pitch and a 152px field is a share of a 331px line it cannot afford (6rem holds NOT KNOWN, the longest word, at 5.5rem); and the plate wraps rather than breaking `The House` across two lines, the who dropping beneath it at the board's right-hand end with a long speaker name truncating first. Nothing painted shrinks — this is layout, and the Legibility Floor holds.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: The board's one width breakpoint, and the only one that touches every route. The thread becomes a two-column grid — a 7.5rem speaker column and the body — system lines indent 8.6rem to the body column, and the edge token goes from .9rem to 1.4rem. Nothing else changes; there is one composition, not two, and below the span nothing moves at all. A content breakpoint, not a device size.

breakpoints.name: admin-columns
breakpoints.purpose: The system's second width breakpoint and its only two-column layout, on /admin alone: minmax(0, 22rem) minmax(0, var(--span)), with health and schedules on the left because they are short and they are where the changing happens, and the feed on the right because it is the long one. Both /admin's grid and its header take the wider --span-admin inset here, or the nameplate centres on one width while the panels under it centre on another.

breakpoints.name: short-screen
breakpoints.purpose: A phone on its side, and a laptop window somebody has squashed. The page is exactly one viewport tall by design, so the header is taking space from the thread rather than competing for it — at 390px tall the board was 43% of the screen. The header padding tightens and the band drops to two devices (`.row:nth-child(n+3) { display: none }`), which is inside what it already is. Nothing that is read changes: the type is untouched and the mark stays at 44px.

breakpoints.name: coarse-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: A capability query, not a width: a laptop with a touchscreen wants this and a 1180px browser window does not. The fader's input becomes 2.75rem tall — the whole groove is the target, since a range input jumps its thumb to wherever the track is touched — and the quiet buttons, the nameplate link and the steps disclosure each grow a `-0.95rem -0.45rem` ::after reach. Per The Reach Rule nothing painted moves.

breakpoints.name: hover-capable
breakpoints.purpose: A capability query gating every hover state in the system. On a tablet a hover sticks after a tap and leaves the board lit up as though something were still happening. What it holds: the nameplate's underline, the switch button and the admin link going brass, the band's name going full ink, and the quiet buttons going ink — ink and never commanded amber, since a reserved state colour doing decoration is what palette law forbids.

backdrop.name: the-plate
backdrop.value: background-color: #17140A; background-image: url(grain-svg, feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency .85 numOctaves 3, opacity .04), linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 42%, rgba(11, 23, 19, .92) 100%), radial-gradient(ellipse 120% 80% at 50% -10%, #241F12 0%, transparent 60%)
backdrop.purpose: Three layers behind the whole page, in the order a real surface has them: the grain of the enamel, the patina gathering at the foot, and the light falling from above. All three are material rather than decoration, and that is the test any fourth would have to pass. The body is exactly one viewport tall, so the foot of the patina is always the foot of the board.

components.name: The Flap
components.description: The system's atom: a state word on a cool enamel card set into the bronze plate, with the fold drawn behind the lettering and the system's one shadow under it. The word takes the state colour; the card face never does.
components.html: Set Warming Held Quiet Ready

components.description: One device on the board: name, reading, state, on a 1fr auto 9.5rem grid capped at 34rem so the flap column stays a fixed pitch however wide the screen gets. The same row is the atom of the header band, of a device card, of an admin health row and of a schedule row.

components.name: The Plate
components.description: The board's nameplate, worn by every route, ruled underneath with a hairline: where you are, who is speaking, the mark, and a LISTENING / QUIET flap. The name is the way back — there is no navigation bar — and 'switch' is lower case because it is a verb, not a label. The hairline rules the nameplate off from the band beneath it, so it is absent when the plate is the only thing in the board — on /house and /admin it would otherwise rule the name off from nothing, a hairline and the board's 2px brass edge with a void between them.

The House·Devices

components.name: The Card
components.description: A board row that grew a control. Same three columns, same vocabulary, same pitch (34rem) — what a card adds is the room underneath the row. Separated by a hairline rule and padding rather than a border, a fill or a shadow: a card is not a panel. One column on every viewport, sitting in the centred span with the nameplate rather than hugging the left edge of the screen.

components.name: The Fader
components.description: The setpoint control, and the only place in this house where a fat finger actuates something. The groove is cut into the plate — groove material, a groove-edge line on top and a seam-light line under it, the same construction as the flap's fold — and the travelled part is brass-dim. The thumb is a machined slug in three layers: a witness line, the knurl, and brass falling from brass-lit at the top edge to brass-shade at the bottom. The asking label rides the thumb in commanded amber and is on the board only while a finger is down. Under a coarse pointer the input is 2.75rem tall and the slug, the lettering and the ends are untouched: the area that answers a finger grows and nothing painted moves. The asking label rides the slug's travel and not the track's: a range input slides the slug's centre across a track shortened by one slug, so a flat percentage is half a slug adrift at each end. Under a coarse pointer only the height changes — nothing painted moves, per The Reach Rule.

72°
60°80°

components.name: The Note
components.description: The board saying what is not there, in the same lettering it uses to say what is: the record voice — condensed uppercase, .74rem, faint ink, capped at the pitch — and the system's only empty-state treatment. Every blank gets one: an empty thread, a house with no devices, a feed with nothing in it, nothing scheduled, nothing schedulable, and the reply that has not arrived — eight lines rotate there, one per turn, all of them the board describing itself. One line, and the strongest true one. A reason inside a note takes declined rust; a filename inside one is lower case in quiet ink, the same exception the plate's `switch` takes.
components.html:
Summoning a word.

Nothing scheduled.

This house has no devices.

Every schedule that can run has a timer.

2 enabled schedules have no timer.

Reading house.exs
components.css: .ds-note { margin: 0; max-width: 34rem; font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Avenir Next Condensed", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .07em; font-size: .74rem; color: var(--ink-faint, #8A9C92); } .ds-note .ds-wrong { color: var(--st-refused, #D2604A); } .ds-note .ds-file { text-transform: none; letter-spacing: .04em; color: var(--ink-quiet, #9AABA1); }

components.name: The Blank
components.description: The empty thread, sitting where the first line will land, and the one place the board says something about what to do next. Dobby does not fill this space — proactive speech is a deferred decision and a greeting here would take it quietly. What fills it is a note in the record voice and then a household utterance: a person's sentence in Barlow at body scale, quoted, in quiet ink. The two faces do the telling. The specimen is built from a snapshot — a device that has actually reported, at a value inside the range it gave us — and is omitted entirely before the house has spoken. Before a name, one line instead, saying what a name is for.
components.html:
Nothing said yet.

Something like “put the main thermostat to 70”
components.css: .ds-blank { --ds-span: 42.6rem; --ds-edge: .9rem; display: grid; gap: .3rem; padding: 0 max(var(--ds-edge), calc((100% - var(--ds-span)) / 2)) .9rem; } .ds-blank .ds-like { display: flex; align-items: baseline; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .55rem; } .ds-blank .ds-said { font-family: Barlow, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; text-transform: none; letter-spacing: normal; font-size: 1rem; color: var(--ink-quiet, #9AABA1); } @media (min-width: 820px) { .ds-blank { --ds-edge: 1.4rem; padding-block: 0 1.1rem; } }

components.name: The Undo Line
components.description: The system's alternative to a confirm dialog: do it, then offer a way back for eight seconds. The button — transparent, no border but a 1px brass-dim underline, brass lettering, lower case — is the system's quiet control, and the same treatment carries pause, resume, delete and the form's Add. A refusal is not an undo: HELD and its reason stay until the next attempt.

components.name: System Line
components.description: The intervention record: what changed in the house, by whatever path. Ruled above and below with hairlines, condensed uppercase, the device name in full ink because it is the content of the line and the via half in faint ink. The word is always SET, or HELD for a device that declined; a refusal's reason takes its own line in sentence case and declined rust. Indents to the body column at 820px.

components.name: The Set Line
components.description: The composer as the board's set line: a transparent input on the raised rail, no border, a 2px brass rule above it, and a brass send arrow behind a hairline divider. The placeholder is condensed uppercase, deliberately a label rather than a sentence. The caret is commanded amber and focus-visible draws a 2px amber ring — the one global interactive state in the system. It does not focus itself on mount. A browser matches :focus-visible on any focused text input however the focus arrived, so an autofocusing composer makes that ring the board's resting state rather than a response to anybody.

components.name: Feed Row
components.description: The full record on /admin: a fixed five-column grid — time, kind, what, who, took — hairline-ruled between entries, in the record voice. Fixed pitch so a streaming log does not shift its columns under a reader; what and who truncate rather than wrap, and took is right-aligned. Three registers in five columns: the time, the kind and the actor are labels and take capitals; `what` carries an entity id and an action name and is set in lower case per The Identifier Rule. The kind's stored underscore is spaced rather than shown.

components.css: .ds-feed { min-width: 0; } .ds-entry { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 5.5rem 6.5rem minmax(0, 1fr) 7rem 3.5rem; gap: .5rem; align-items: baseline; padding: .18rem 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule, #2E2A1A); font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Avenir Next Condensed", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .05em; font-size: .74rem; color: var(--ink-quiet, #9AABA1); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-entry .ds-t, .ds-entry .ds-took { color: var(--ink-faint, #8A9C92); } .ds-entry .ds-what { color: var(--ink, #E8E2D2); text-transform: none; letter-spacing: .04em; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-entry .ds-kind, .ds-entry .ds-who, .ds-entry .ds-what { white-space: nowrap; } .ds-entry .ds-who { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-entry .ds-took { text-align: right; }

components.name: Utterance
components.description: One line of the household thread, and the largest text on the surface: the only thing set in Barlow at reading scale, capped at 62ch. Speaker in brass condensed uppercase, time in faint ink — inline above on phone, a fixed 7.5rem column at 820px. Never aligned, indented or coloured by author.
components.html:
greg4:12 PM

set the thermostat to 70
components.css: .ds-msg { margin-bottom: 1.05rem; } .ds-attr { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: .55rem; margin-bottom: .12rem; } .ds-attr .ds-sp { font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Avenir Next Condensed", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .09em; font-size: .74rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--brass, #B08A46); } .ds-attr .ds-t { font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Avenir Next Condensed", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: .74rem; color: var(--ink-faint, #8A9C92); letter-spacing: .05em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-said { margin: 0; font-family: Barlow, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 1.12rem; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--ink, #E8E2D2); max-width: 62ch; } @media (min-width: 820px) { .ds-msg { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 7.5rem 1fr; gap: 0 1.1rem; align-items: baseline; } .ds-attr { flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: .05rem; margin: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
A split-flap board can only display what it was set to. It cannot show a state
nobody commanded. That mechanical fact is the whole system: Dobby is forbidden
to claim a room got warm when all that happened was a command being accepted,
and the surface enforces the same honesty in its materials rather than in a
paragraph of prose. Every state on this board is a word on a flap, and a word
had to be set by somebody.

The world is a magical household instrument — enamel ground, brass rules,
painted lettering — not a wizard. It is alive and honest rather than ornate.
Register was pinned as fun, hearted and magical (direction round, 2026-08-14).
A write-up of that pin hardened it into "no wizarding diction", which Greg
reopened on 2026-08-16: the board is allowed to be a little magical about its
own workings — see The Note. What holds is narrower and it is about *whose*
magic. The object is alive; Dobby is not a wizard. No trademarked franchise
asset appears anywhere and none ever will — the product is named Dobby, and a
house-elf's name plus a wizard's vocabulary is the one combination that reads
as a franchise rather than as a world.

Density is low and deliberate. The board carries two or three device rows and
then gets out of the way; the conversation below it is set at reading scale
because what a person said is the material this product is made of. The
record-keeping — steps, timings, system lines — is what gets small.

Confirmed anti-references: the dark card grid with a circular dial, which
shows a number and tells you nothing about who set it or whether it took;
parchment, wax-seal and filigree pastiche; any trademarked franchise mark.
keyCharacteristics: Words on flaps, never icons and never bare numbers
Five reserved state colours and no sixth
Square corners everywhere; the only curve is the drawing of Dobby himself
Two hue families — a green-black enamel ground and warm brass-and-cream ink
Flat by default; one shadow in the entire system
Fixed-pitch columns and tabular figures, so a changing number does not shift
One board width on every route; past it the board centres rather than stretches
Every blank says what it is, in the record voice

rules.name: The Palette Law
rules.body: Five reserved state colours, each meaning exactly one thing, used decoratively nowhere. A sixth state colour is a design change, not a CSS change. Audit test: search the stylesheet for a state colour outside a `[data-st]` selector, a tick, a refusal reason, or one of the four sanctioned sites listed below — there should be none.

rules.name: The Edges Rule
rules.body: State colour lives on ink, rules, ticks and flap edges — never as a tint behind readable text.

rules.name: The Night Kitchen Rule
rules.body: A screen left on in a kitchen must not light the room at 11pm. Audit test: open the board in a dark room. If it reads as a lamp rather than a sign, the saturation is wrong.

rules.name: Language Is The Material
rules.body: What a person said gets board-scale type, not chat-bubble type in 14px grey. The record-keeping around it is what gets small. Audit test: in any thread screenshot, the largest text should be somebody's sentence.

rules.name: The Legibility Floor
rules.body: Type is sized by reading distance and never shrinks to fit. Content reflows or truncates; type does not scale down. There is no responsive font-size anywhere in the system and adding one is a change to this rule, not to a component.

rules.name: The Instrument Voice Rule
rules.body: The condensed face is only ever the board speaking about itself — states, names, times, steps. Dobby's own words are never set in it.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Capitals on this board mean a label — a state, a name, a time. An identifier is not a label: an entity id, an action name, a schema key or a filename is a thing you go and open, and it is set in the condensed face in lower case, `.arg`. The health panel had always done this and the three things beside it had not, so one page printed `thermostat:main` in one panel and `THERMOSTAT:MAIN` in the next. Audit test: search the surface for a shouted underscore — an identifier is the only string here that has one.

rules.name: The Shared Document Rule
rules.body: Nothing is ever aligned or positioned by author. The thread is a household record, and positioning a message by who is holding the phone means two people reading the same conversation see two different documents. Audit test: two browsers, two names, one screenshot each — the messages must land in the same place.

rules.name: The No Nav Rule
rules.body: Navigation is carried by things that already exist — the nameplate, the band of rows, one quiet link at the foot of a page. A shell of links around this would be a second visual language arguing with the first. Audit test: no route may introduce a nav element; a new page earns its way in from a surface that already leads somewhere.

rules.name: The One Width Rule
rules.body: A board has one width, and a rule stops where the content under it stops. The plate used to span the viewport while everything beneath it stopped at the pitch, which on an iPad in landscape is a 522px board under a 1180px rule — past about 900px that stops reading as restraint and starts reading as a page that failed to load. The two brass rails are the named exception, because they are the board's edges. Audit test: open any route at 1440px; every left edge on the page should fall on the same line, and no rule should be more than the span wide.

rules.name: The Reach Rule
rules.body: A target grows by reach, not by box. Where a finger needs more than the drawing gives it, the area that answers grows and nothing visible moves — the slug keeps its 13px, the lettering keeps its size, the underline stays under its word. Audit test: no `pointer: coarse` rule may change a font-size, a stroke, or the position of anything painted.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: The flap has the only `box-shadow` in the system. Anything else that wants depth gets a tonal step or a brass rule instead.

rules.name: The Material Rule
rules.body: Every colour in the system belongs to one of three materials — the bronze plate, the enamel cards, the brass-and-cream ink — or to a state. A colour that belongs to none of them has no business here, and that is the question to ask of any addition: *what is it made of?* It is also the reason the cool green survived the plate going warm. It was not kept because it was liked; it was given a job — the cards, and the oxidation — and a colour with a job is material, while the same colour used for emphasis would have been a second green two shades from Acting Green, on a board whose whole argument is that a colour means exactly one thing.

rules.name: The Fold Rule
rules.body: The fold is drawn *behind* the lettering, never across it. A seam over the glyphs reads as a strikethrough, and a struck word means cancelled — which would be a lie about every state on this board.

rules.name: The Words Rule
rules.body: A state is a word. Adding an icon, a dot, a badge or a bare number to say what a word already says is a regression, not a refinement.

rules.name: The Commanded-Not-Observed Rule
rules.body: `SET` means a value was commanded. `WARMING` means the house reported the device acting on it. The board never infers a state from a reading alone, because that is precisely the lie Dobby is forbidden to tell.

rules.name: The Affirmative Loud Rule
rules.body: The affirmative states are the loud ones. Refusal is `HELD`, quietly, with its reason beside it — never a punchline in the reserved red. A design that leads with refusal is selling the wrong product.

rules.name: The Absent Word Rule
rules.body: When no word in the vocabulary is true of a row, the row gets no flap. A paused schedule shows none: nothing among the eight means "somebody switched this off" — `QUIET` is an endpoint that stopped answering and `HELD` is a device declining — and bending either to fit would put a word on the board that means two things. The row goes faint and its button says `resume`, which says it without a word. A ninth word is a design decision, not a CSS change.

rules.name: The Uncommanded Value Rule
rules.body: A value somebody is still choosing is never written into a reading. It may sit beside the control, in commanded amber, for as long as the hand is on it, and it leaves the board the moment the board takes over. Audit test: release the fader with the house slow to answer — nothing on the card should show the new number until the house has confirmed it.

dos: Do say a state in a word from the vocabulary above, on a flap.
Do give a new state a new word before giving it a new colour. Five reserved colours, and a sixth is a design decision.
Do put state colour on ink, ticks, rules and edges.
Do set anything a person said in Barlow at 1.12rem, and everything the instrument says about itself in Barlow Condensed uppercase.
Do keep corners square. The only curves in the world are Dobby.
Do use tabular figures for every number, so a changing reading does not shift the column beside it.
Do draw the fold behind the lettering.
Do distinguish "not answering" from "not yet known". They are different facts and the vocabulary has a word for each.
Do leave the flap off entirely when none of the eight words is true. Silence is a legitimate answer; a bent word is not.
Do answer a destructive action with an undo line for a few seconds, instead of a confirm dialog.
Do commit a drag on release, and show what is being asked for beside the control rather than in the reading.
Do answer an empty region with a line in the record voice. A heading over a void is the board declining to answer.
Do finish the sentence when a list it names is empty — "this house has no devices", never "this house has:" and nothing.
Do grow the area a finger hits, and leave the drawing exactly where it is.
Do keep every left edge on a page on one line, and stop a rule where the content under it stops.
Do set an identifier in lower case. Capitals are a state, a name or a time.
Do say what a blank is even when the blank is a wait. The reply that has not arrived is a blank like any other, and it is the one a household sees most.
donts: Don't put a tint behind readable text, in any colour.
Don't add a `border-radius` to a flap, an input, a button, or a panel.
Don't add a second `box-shadow`. Depth is tonal.
Don't align, indent or colour a message by who said it.
Don't shrink type to make content fit. Reflow or truncate instead.
Don't render the mark below 40px, and don't use the ears without the head.
Don't phrase a step as Dobby speaking ("Let me just check the thermostat…"). Steps are labels in device language, and the soul bans process narration in his voice.
Don't use franchise assets or parchment-and-wax-seal pastiche. The product is named Dobby and that is exactly why: this world has to earn "magical" rather than borrow it.

Don't put magic in Dobby's mouth. The board may be magical about its own workings — it is a magical instrument. Dobby is a capable person who lives here, his voice is a tested file, and it stays plain.
Don't add a navigation bar. The nameplate, the band and one quiet link are the navigation.
Don't write a value a person is still choosing into a device's reading.
Don't widen an existing state word to cover a new case. Add a word, or leave the flap off.
Don't turn the cards page into a grid of tiles. One column at the pitch, on every viewport.
Don't fill an empty thread with Dobby greeting anybody. Proactive speech is a deferred decision and this is where it gets taken by accident.
Don't name a device or a value in a specimen sentence that the house has not reported. Build it from a snapshot or leave it out.
Don't let a container run to the viewport. The board has one width, and past the span it centres.
Don't change a font-size, a stroke, or the position of anything painted inside a `pointer: coarse` block.
Don't leave an interactive element in the tab order when it has nothing in it. An empty band is no band.
Don't focus an input on mount. A browser draws a focus ring on a focused text input however the focus arrived, and a ring nobody asked for becomes the page's resting state.
Don't shout an entity id, an action name or a schema key. See The Identifier Rule.
Don't put anything in the timestamp slot that is not a time. An ellipsis there reads as a clock that failed, not as a board at work.
